chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Washshāʾ, who said:
I heard al-Riḍā عليه السلام saying: “Indeed, the deeds are presented to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, their righteous ones and their wicked ones.”

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام, the speaker of this hadith
key_terms.الْأَعْمَالَ: the deeds and actions performed by people
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ai.seo_question: Are people's deeds presented to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the deeds of people are presented to Rasūl Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, including both righteous and sinful deeds. It indicates an ongoing connection between the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and the deeds of the community, and highlights accountability before Allah through this presentation.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Washha who said,
‘I heard Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The deeds get presented to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, its righteous ones and its immoral ones’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ who has said the following.
“I heard Imam al-Rida saying, ‘All the deeds: good and bad ones are presented before the Messenger of Allah.’”
